parts.problem_md:
Steve is asked to solve the equation $5 ( x + 2 ) = 47$

Here is his working.

$\begin{gathered} 5 ( x + 2 ) & = 47 \\ 5 x + 2 & = 47 \\ 5 x & = 45 \\ x & = 9 \end{gathered}$

Steve's answer is wrong.

What mistake did he make?
parts.solution_md:
> *The second line of Steve's working involved expanding out single brackets. *

> *You must expand **both parts** of the brackets.*

$\begin{gathered} 5 ( x + 2 ) & = 47 \\ 5 x + 10 & = 47 \end{gathered}$

**Steve did not expand the second part of the brackets**** [1]**

> *Start by expanding the bracket on the left-hand side. Remember to expand both parts of the bracket.*

$\begin{gathered} 5 ( 4 - x ) & = 7 - 3 x \\ 20 - 5 x & = 7 - 3 x \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Bring the **x** terms to one side by adding the term with the smallest coefficient of **x **(-5**x**).  *

$\begin{gathered} 20 - 5 x & = 7 - 3 x \\ + 5 x & = + 5 x \\ 20 & = 7 + 2 x \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Subtract 7 from both sides.*

$13=2x$

> *Divide both sides by 2.*

$\frac{13}{2}=x$

$x=\frac{13}{2}\mathrm{or}6.5$ **[1]**

**It's a good idea to check your answer by using your calculator to substitute it into the original equation, as below**

$\begin{gathered} 5 ( 4 - 6.5 ) & = 7 - 3 ( 6.5 ) \\ \text{LHS} : 5 ( 4 - 6.5 ) & = - 12.5 \\ \text{RHS} : 7 - 3 ( 6.5 ) & = - 12.5 \end{gathered}$

*(Left Hand Side matched Right Hand Side therefore correct)*

$\begin{gathered} 10 ( \frac{4 x - 1}{5} ) + 10 ( \frac{x + 4}{2} ) & = 10 ( 3 ) \end{gathered}$

* ***[1]**

> *Simplify by cancelling each fraction. *

> *The fractions should disappear.*

$\begin{gathered} 8 x + 5 x - 2 + 20 & = 30 \\ 13 x + 18 & = 30 \end{gathered}$

> *Subtract 18 from both sides.*

$\begin{gathered} 13 x & = 30 - 18 \\ 13 x & = 12 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 13.*

$\begin{gathered} 12 ( \frac{x + 1}{3} ) + 12 ( \frac{2 x + 5}{4} ) & = 12 ( 2 ) \end{gathered}$

* ***[1]**

> *The fractions should disappear.*

$\begin{gathered} \cancel{12 ( \frac{x + 1}{ \cancel{3} } ) + \cancel{ } 12} ( \frac{2 x + 5}{ \cancel{4} } ) & = 12 ( 2 ) \\ 4 ( x + 1 ) + 3 ( 2 x + 5 ) & = 24 \end{gathered}$

> *Simplify the left hand side by bringing the **x** terms together and the number terms together.*

$\begin{array}{rcl} 4 x + 6 x + 4 + 15 & = 24 \\ 10 x + 19 & = 24 \end{array}$

> *Subtract 19 from both sides.*

$\begin{array}{rcl} 10 x & = 24 - 19 \\ 10 x & = 5 \end{array}$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 10.*

$\begin{gathered} 6 x ( \frac{x + 2}{3 x} ) + 6 x ( \frac{x - 2}{2 x} ) & = 6 x ( 3 ) \end{gathered}$

* ***[1]**

> *Simplify by cancelling the common terms in each fraction. *

$\begin{gathered} \cancel{6 x} ( \frac{x + 2}{ \cancel{3 x} } ) + \cancel{6 x} ( \frac{x - 2}{ \cancel{2 x} } ) & = 6 x ( 3 ) \\ 2 ( x + 2 ) + 3 ( x - 2 ) & = 18 x \end{gathered}$

> *Expand both sets of brackets on the left-hand side. *

$\begin{array}{rcl} 2 x + 4 + 3 x - 6 & = 18 x \end{array}$

> *Simplify the left hand side by bringing the **x** terms together and the number terms together.*

$\begin{gathered} 2 x + 3 x + 4 - 6 & = 18 x \\ 5 x - 2 & = 18 x \end{gathered}$

> *Bring the **x** terms to one side by subtracting 5**x** from both sides.*

$\begin{gathered} - 2 & = 18 x - 5 x \\ 13 x & = - 2 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 13.*

$x=\frac{-2}{13}$

$\begin{gathered} 6 ( \frac{h + 7}{3} ) + 6 ( \frac{2 h - 1}{2} ) & = 6 ( \frac{5}{6} ) \end{gathered}$

* ***[1]**

* ***[1]**

> *Simplify the left hand side by bringing the **h** terms together and the number terms together.*

$\begin{gathered} 2 h + 6 h + 14 - 3 & = 5 \\ 8 h + 11 & = 5 \end{gathered}$

> *Subtract 11 from both sides.*

$\begin{gathered} 8 h & = 5 - 11 \\ 8 h & = - 6 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 8.*

$h=-\frac{6}{8}=-\frac{3}{4}$

> *Remove the fractions by multiplying every term by the lowest common denominator. *

> *The lowest common denominator is the LCM of 4, 3 and 6 = 12.*

$\begin{gathered} 12 ( \frac{3 x - 2}{4} ) - 12 ( \frac{2 x + 5}{3} ) & = 12 ( \frac{1 - x}{6} ) \end{gathered}$

* ***[1]**

> *Simplify by cancelling the common terms in each fraction. The fractions should disappear.*

$\begin{array}{rcl} \cancel{12} ( \frac{3 x - 2}{ \cancel{4} } ) - \cancel{12} ( \frac{2 x + 5}{ \cancel{3} } ) & = \cancel{12} ( \frac{1 - x}{ \cancel{6} } ) \\ 3 ( 3 x - 2 ) - 4 ( 2 x + 5 ) & = 2 ( 1 - x ) \end{array}$

* ***[1]**

> *Expand all three sets of brackets. *

> *Remember to expand both parts of the bracket and be careful with the negative sign.*

$\begin{gathered} 9 x - 6 - 8 x - 20 & = 2 - 2 x \end{gathered}$

> *Simplify the left hand side.*

$\begin{gathered} 9 x - 8 x - 6 - 20 & = 2 - 2 x \\ x - 26 & = 2 - 2 x \end{gathered}$

> *Bring the **x** terms to one side by adding 2**x** to both sides and the number terms to the other by adding 26 to both sides.*

$\begin{gathered} x - 26 & = 2 - 2 x \\ + 2 x & = + 2 x \\ 3 x - 26 & = 2 \\ + 26 & = + 26 \\ 3 x & = 28 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 3.*

$x=\frac{28}{3}$

$x=9\frac{1}{3}$ **[1]**

**The improper fraction is also accepted. **

$4x^{2}+10x+10x+25=4x^{2}-2x+6x-3$

**[1]**

$4x^{2}+20x+25=4x^{2}+4x-3$

$\begin{gathered} 4 x^{2} + 20 x + 25 & = 4 x^{2} + 4 x - 3 \\ - 4 x^{2 } & = - 4 x^{2} \\ 20 x + 25 & = 4 x - 3 \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

parts.problem_md:
The functions $f$and $g$ are defined as

$\begin{gathered} \mathrm{f} ( x ) & = x^{2} + 6 \\ \mathrm{g} ( x ) & = x - 10 \end{gathered}$

Solve the equation $\mathrm{fg}(x)=f(x)$

Show clear algebraic working.
parts.solution_md:
> *Although this may at first appear to be a quadratic equations question, it's actually a linear equations question "in disguise"!*

> *First rewrite *$\text{fg} ( x ) = \mathrm{f} ( x )$* in terms of *$x$* using composite functions.*

$( x - 10 )^{2} + 6 = x^{2} + 6$

**[1]**

> *Expand the brackets; *$( x - 10 )^{2} = ( x - 10 ) ( x - 10 )$*.*

$x^{2}-20x+100+6=x^{2}+6$

**[1]**

> *Collect like terms on the left hand side.*

$x^{2}-20x+106=x^{2}+6$

> *Now subtract *$x^{2}$* from both sides, to reveal the linear equation!*

$\begin{gathered} x^{2} - 20 x + 106 & = x^{2} + 6 \\ - x^{2} & = - x^{2} \\ - 20 x + 106 & = 6 \end{gathered}$

> *Subtract 106 from both sides.*

$\begin{gathered} - 20 x & = - 100 \end{gathered}$

> *And divide both sides by -20.*

$\begin{gathered} x & = \frac{- 100}{- 20} = 5 \end{gathered}$

$x=5$ ** [1]**
